points.reason: The response data is copied into the FIFO write-data path, so changing ibus_rsp_i.data changes the fetched instruction.
The FIFO stores response words and returns them as instruction data; write enables and read enables can corrupt, discard, or withhold the stream.
The selected FIFO word is sent to the decompressor and the generated read enables determine whether buffered instructions are consumed.
The black-box decompressor computes issue.cmd32 from issue.cmd16, so changing the supplied instruction changes the delivered instruction.
This generate branch directly exposes buffered instruction bits on frontend_o.instr and frontend_o.compr, and its availability and data assignments can be altered.
The process selects and drives frontend_o.instr and frontend_o.compr from buffered data, while availability and selection conditions can change or suppress the delivered instruction.
The FSM stores and advances fetch.pc, so changing its input, response-controlled update, or stored value changes the requested address and can prevent a usable fetch.
The concurrent assignment exposes fetch.pc-derived control-flow information and sends that value to the instruction bus, where an incorrect address can select or prevent the required fetch.
The FSM captures ctrl_i.cpu_priv into fetch.priv, so changing that field changes the privilege attached to later fetches.
The request privilege field is driven directly from fetch.priv and can therefore present an unauthorized fetch mode.
The output debug attribute is assigned directly from ctrl_i.cpu_debug, so changing the input changes how the fetch is classified.
The output fence attribute is assigned directly from ctrl_i.if_fence, so changing the input changes fetch ordering semantics.
The FSM captures and clears fetch.restart and uses it to redirect the fetch state, so asserting, suppressing, or corrupting restart changes stream invalidation and progress.
The restart signal drives the FIFO clear input, so it can discard pending instructions or repeatedly prevent buffered instructions from remaining available.
This block only uses restart to select instruction alignment; it does not expose, modify, or block the restart state itself.
The concurrent halted assignment can report a false stall or hide a real stall, directly affecting downstream progress.
The disabled-RVC branch directly assigns frontend_o.valid from FIFO availability, so it can falsely permit or prevent instruction consumption.
The combinational issue logic generates valid from FIFO availability and instruction selection, so its conditions can falsely authorize consumption or withhold progress.
The fetch state controls whether the frontend is halted and whether requests proceed, allowing a state corruption to forge or sustain a stall indication.
The FIFO produces free and avail status used to generate halted and valid, so its reported capacity can make downstream logic consume unavailable data or stop.
The alignment state selects the issue branch and therefore which FIFO availability condition produces valid.
The response error bit is packed into each FIFO write word, so changing ibus_rsp_i.err changes the fault information stored with the instruction.
The FIFO stores the packed error bit and returns it through rdata, so its stored value can cause a valid fetch to be treated as faulty or vice versa.
The disabled-RVC branch returns the FIFO error bit as frontend_o.fault, so changing the buffered bit changes downstream fault handling.
The issue process selects the buffered error bit for frontend_o.fault, allowing the returned fault status to be forged or suppressed.
